parameters.content:
## Back up n8n workflows to GitHub

Keeps every workflow of your instance in a private GitHub repo, with one commit per run and nothing written when nothing changed.

### How it works

The workflow pulls every workflow from the n8n API, archived ones included, and turns each into a JSON file. Volatile fields like updatedAt and versionId are stripped and keys are sorted, so a workflow you did not touch produces the same bytes as yesterday.

The whole set goes to GitHub through the Git Data API as one tree, which becomes one commit. If that tree matches what the branch already points at, the run stops and nothing is written.

### Setup steps

- Private repo, initialised with a README. An empty repo has no branch to read
- GitHub fine-grained token scoped to that repo, Contents read and write
- n8n API key from Settings, in an n8n API credential on List workflows
- The GitHub credential on the six HTTP Request nodes
- Fill owner, repo, branch and folder in Configuration
- Run it twice. The second run should commit nothing

### Customization

Switch to a six hour schedule if losing a day of changes is too much. Point it at a dedicated branch to review changes through pull requests. If a field keeps changing between runs, add it to the VOLATILE list in Normalise workflows.

### Collect and normalise

Every workflow comes from the n8n API, archived ones included. Volatile fields are stripped and keys sorted, so untouched workflows produce identical files.

### Read the repo state

Where the branch points, which tree that commit carries, and what the repo holds today. That last read is what makes deletions possible.

### Commit only if something changed

One tree carries every file plus the deletions. If its SHA matches the current commit, the IF closes and the run ends. Otherwise one commit lands and the branch moves.

### Before the first run

The repo needs one commit already, otherwise reading the branch returns 404. The token needs Contents read and write: read only passes the three GET calls and fails on the first write.
